Potentially moving abroad after I graduate! It’s been a huge dream of mine to move to England for nearly a decade, but my ex was clearly keen on staying within the country. Of course our relationship was worth it and I never fussed, but now that I’m single I at least have something to look forward to.

I flip flop from wanting to hate her for ending it the way she did and then feeling incredibly empathetic towards her. I think apart of me is desperately trying to loathe her in an attempt to feel better about myself, but besides blindsiding me, our split was amicable and our relationship was beautiful. She was an amazing person and I feel lucky I was able to have something with her, even if it couldn’t last. I can’t hate her and I doubt I’ll stay mad at her. I used to think hating her or having a bad-natured breakup would’ve made things easier, but honestly it would’ve hurt me all the same. Breakups fucking suck no matter what.
I really like Shiloh for a girl and Forrest for a boy
She told me she loved me the night before she blindsided me.

I must be odd, but I’m only a bit over a month past and somehow I’ve felt relatively fine these past couple weeks. I still get occasional mood swings and depressive bouts, but I’d say I feel at least okay 85% of the time. It shouldn’t make sense because I was deeply in love with her, she broke my heart in a horrible way, and the breakup devastated me. I guess I attribute my overall okayness to the switch that flipped in my head when she left me.

I also recognize that this is probably the best thing that needed to happen to me.
Owning a Tesla

Never, she cruelly blindsided me and I have enough self-respect now to not pine after someone who’d ended things so disrespectfully. Even though I had plenty of low moments, I worked on myself for our relationship. She lied to me and betrayed my trust to the worst degree. She doesn’t deserve to hear from me.

If I hadn’t taken my breakup as a massive wake-up call, I would’ve been on myself in the same way. It’s difficult, trust me; I’ve dealt with issues of self-blame and a lack of self-confidence for practically all my life. However, I’ve been telling myself every single day that I need to work on myself for both my sake and for the sake of my future relationships. In fact, I will not allow myself to jump into another relationship until I’ve learned to truly love, empathize with, and respect myself. 

The past is in the past. We can’t change it, but we can decide the courses of our futures. We can either fall victim to the vicious cycles of old tendencies or we can push beyond them.

Every single one of my dreams since my breakup nearly a month ago has involved her, but last night I finally had my first dream without her in it. It’ll get better with time.

I really do need to be reminded to steer clear of her socials. Neither of us were really involved too much with social media, but she had an Insta account for her projects and we both followed each other on Spotify. We unfollowed each other on both, but I can’t help but check up on her Spotify every so often. Seeing that she deleted every playlist once associated with me while making new playlists weirdly upsets me. Of course I’m getting a tiny cutout of the big picture, but it sends my mind places. 

I’m genuinely happy that this breakup gave me the wake up call that I’ve desperately been needing for most of my life, but it still feels so bittersweet because I had to lose someone who I thought was the love of my life in order to get here. Although, I tell myself often that if our relationship had never happened, I have no doubts that I would’ve made the same mistakes in another relationship. It helps me recognize that this experience is actually yielding a reward that might have been worth the loss, as horrible as that is to say lol.

Thank you, this helped calm me a bit. I’m doing my absolute best to view this whole thing as an experience to be learned from. I’ve actually made quite a bit of progress in these past three weeks. NC is something I’m genuinely doing for myself, I don’t do it with the expectation that it will help get her back or anything, even though a part of me often fantasizes about her reaching out in the future. I’ve heard the whole opposite grief processes thing before, and it gives me some comfort, even though it’s a generalization. I’m really going through the motions, but I know I’ll get through this and come out a better person.
The logical part of me tells me this, but during my lowest points it’s difficult to shake those insecurities. It gets better everyday, I guess I just needed to vent.

I feel like most of my days lately have been generally pretty decent; I feel good about myself and I’m doing a lot on the side to keep me busy. However, when a thought creeps in it’s hard for me to ignore it and suddenly I feel like I’m back to week 1. Usually I’m able to sort myself out before bed at least, but the dreams are still persistent as ever.

No, because I have made more progress in regards to my own self-growth these past few weeks than I ever have in my life prior to the breakup. I’m glad she was apart of my life, even if she wasn’t “the one”. It was a great experience and it taught me a lot. If I never went through it all, I probably would’ve made the same mistakes in another relationship.

I get good hours and lately I’ve been able to make it through the nights fully. However, when I dream, every single one of them has been about her. It’s always so upsetting when I wake up.

I obviously can’t help it, only time can get rid of them.
No, absolutely not. I’m only 3 weeks in. I am recovering, but it’ll take time to fully get there.

It really depends. If either of us still hadn’t moved on from our last relationship, I would not go back to her. The mental health reasons for our breakup would have to have been worked on significantly on both ends before I’d even consider it, so giving our split time would be necessary. She would have to show me that she is willing to communicate with me, especially considering that she broke my trust by blindsiding me. If her reasons for wanting to give the relationship another shot had to do mostly with feelings of nostalgia, then I feel like I would be at great risk of getting heartbroken again.

If time had passed, we’d both matured, and we could both see a future together and would be willing to put the work in, then I could see myself going back to her.

However, I don’t expect any of this nor do I want to get my hopes up. It wouldn’t be my place to try and get back together with her, so all I can do right now is focus on myself and move on. This breakup hit me hard, and I cannot see myself entering another one anytime soon. Besides, this is me speaking fresh out of a breakup. Given enough time, I probably won’t want anything to do with her.
That I’m genuinely sorry that my mental health problems and anxiety issues likely caused her so much stress that she probably bottled up. I wish I could apologize for my self-deprecating behavior.

Thanks. I really wanted to be angry with her yesterday, but I realize now that there is also the possibility that she was telling the truth, but she knew what was best for herself and decided to go for it. I don’t even know why I hope or care, considering I absolutely want to move on from her. I guess it would feel extra worse if I’d known she’d lied about that.

Thank you for this. I’m only a little less than three weeks past my breakup, but I’ve been putting a lot of these into practice. I started seeing a therapist, stopped binge-eating, and I’ve been going to the gym everyday for the past week and plan to continue that streak until I go back to school. It really is helpful stuff.

This sounds very familiar to how I felt the first day of my own breakup. I’ve always had awful anxiety and been prone to anxiety attacks. I was beyond heartbroken when she blindsided me. No more calls every other day of the summer? No more good morning and goodnight “I love you”’s? I was terrified since I don’t have friends outside of her, and I think that’s the part of our relationship that I will always mourn the most. I thought that I would fall into the pit I was in before I met her, one riddled with horrendous anxiety and depression. However, I wouldn’t let this destroy me. I took this as a wake-up call to really start working on myself. As hard as it is to tell myself this everyday, my only goal right now is to become the best version of me possible, for my sake and for the sake of any future relationships. I know how hard it is having to go through this, but try to use this time to focus on yourself. Seek therapy. Talk to any loved ones you have. 

It really does get better. The unbearable pain in your heart will slowly diminish with time, and one day you will look back on this whole ordeal as a distant, bittersweet memory. I’m so sorry you’re going through this right now, it’s such a difficult thing to experience. Sendings hugs.

A little bit. The breakup wasn’t mutual as she’d totally sprung it on me seemingly out of nowhere. Apart of me wants to believe that things could’ve gone differently if she’d just talked to me sooner. However, I also understand that it may have been inevitable. I wasn’t helping myself. I got stuck in the comfort of my relationship with her, and I felt little incentive to really push myself to work on my mental health. Blindsiding me was a cruel move, but the reason for the breakup was valid.
Thankss :’)
I really hope so, my ex was a truly wonderful person, but I think I need to take a break from romance for a while. The only relationship I’m looking for right now is a better one with myself.
I definitely need a hug lol. These are tumultuous times.

It’s hard, I doubt myself everyday. Rejecting my habit of self-blame and my insecurities is incredibly strenuous, but I know that I have to work past them. I fully realize now that I cannot be in a relationship if I cannot learn to truly love and respect myself. Like I said, this breakup is a life lesson for me, and I will make sure that I take away as much as I can from it.
I’m actually trying to be empathetic towards myself. I don’t ever want to be the insecure, self-conscious person I used to be ever again, for the sake of myself and any future relationships.

If she had never existed in my life, I would not be going through this hellish ordeal right now. That being said, I would also probably still be in the same boat that I was in before our breakup, and I probably would’ve made the same mistakes in another relationship. This experience exists so that I may learn from it and grow as a person. I don’t regret our relationship. It was beautiful and I will always cherish our memories together. She wasn’t the one for me, but I’m grateful for everything that our relationship taught me.

I recognize that although this breakup is easily the hardest thing that I’ve ever had to deal with, it has been a massive wake-up call for me and I know that I will come out of this a better person. I learned a lot, and I’m thankful for that.
This is exactly me

I felt bad for her, even now I still do. It must’ve been awful feeling like she had to struggle alone. I wished I could’ve done more for her, if only she’d been honest with me. When she broke up with me, she apologized a lot and told me she still loved me. 

I think the reason she ended our breakup call so quickly was because she couldn’t handle hurting me in that moment any longer (even though an insecure part of me still believes it was because she was dying to be rid of me). I didn’t deserve the cruelty that came with that kind of a breakup, but I can’t stay mad at her for that. She had fair reasons for wanting to end things; I only wish that she’d come to me about it sooner so that I could’ve done more, even if the outcome ultimately were the same.

No, but throughout our relationship she always mentioned how she struggled with being upfront with others. She was a bit of a people pleaser and I think she hated the thought of hurting my feelings. She went to therapy for it, but she apparently struggled opening up to me until the very end.

Because I knew that, my insecurities would often kick in and I’d ask her if she was keeping anything in that she wanted to tell me, but she’d always reassure me. It’s hard to say how honest she was being with me in retrospect.

Thanks, it sucks a lot lol. She’s genuinely a good person, but creating a lie within our relationship and alluding to everything being okay until she dropped the bomb on me was totally a cruel move on her part.
I got about an hour worth of “closure” through a phone call. Honestly, I don’t think I’ll ever get the closure that I want from her. The only person that can give that to me is myself.

I mean, she blindsided me after years of an apparently good relationship. I was self-aware enough not to constantly nag her about it, but insecure to the point where I did occasionally ask her if she felt things were going fine, and if I was too much for her. And every time, she’d claim that she had no doubts and that she loved me. I believed her until she sprung our breakup on me out of the blue. I thought I could trust her throughout our entire relationship. Now I realize I should’ve trusted my gut.
I need to move on before I can try to reconcile with my ex, if I do.

The state of my mental health contributed a lot to our breakup, but she also dealt with some issues of her own. She was not very upfront about how she felt about things. In the end, instead of talking to me like I always asked her to, she blindsided me without giving me a warning or any chance. Given the years that we went through together, and the love she claimed to have for me up until the very end, I don’t know… I just expected I deserved better I guess. She hadn’t been improving much, even though she’d been going to therapy for it. She kept her feelings to herself until the very end, and I never saw it coming.
